title: release(ci): add artifact signing, SBOMs, and release-manifests for private-installer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private require reproducible, auditable release artifacts for on-prem/VPC installs. This PR wires up CI to produce signed release artifacts, SBOMs, and a machine-readable release manifest (provenance) so downstream installers and customers can verify integrity and origin.

Summary of changes: added build steps to the private-installer CI pipeline to emit tarballs and helm chart bundles, generate Syft SBOMs, sign artifacts and SBOMs with cosign, upload signed artifacts and attestations to the release bucket, and synthesize a release-manifest.jsonl file that lists SHA256 checksums, cosign signatures, SBOM links, and build metadata. Also added Terraform module bump and Helm chart packaging tweaks so generated bundles are deterministic between CI runs. Included an end-to-end verify job that pulls artifacts, verifies cosign signatures and SBOM presence, and validates the manifest.

Checklist: - [x] Build artifact packaging for private-installer binary and helm charts - [x] Generate Syft SBOMs (spdx/json and cyclonedx) for each artifact - [x] Sign artifacts and SBOMs with cosign (CI KMS key) - [x] Produce release-manifest (JSONL) with provenance metadata - [x] Upload artifacts, attestation, SBOMs to releases/redwood-private-installer/ - [x] Add verification CI job that validates signatures and checksums - [x] Update Terraform module references for installer release workflow - [x] Documentation: add README for verifying releases locally

Testing and verification: CI runs include unit tests for the packaging scripts, a dry-run packaging job, and an end-to-end verify job that executes cosign verify, syft sbom validation, and manifest checksum comparisons. During the PR we had one transient CI failure when cosign key retrieval timed out; re-running the workflow passed and the verify job succeeded. Manual verification steps are documented in docs/release/verify-local.md.

Rollout plan: This is additive to CI and does not change runtime installer behavior. After merging, the release pipeline will switch to using the new release-manifest and signed artifacts; we'll run a canary release to ensure customers consuming the manifest can validate signatures. Security will rotate the cosign key into production KMS on 2024-12-01 after secret-isolation review.

Notes/constraints: - The cosign key is stored in the org KMS and used by CI; CI uses short-lived signing tokens. - SBOM generation adds a small amount of CI time (~90s per artifact). - Downstream consumers must implement cosign verification and manifest parsing; docs include example scripts.

Related: references previous provenance work in pr-3515 and pr-3568 and aligns with internal SEC/ENG roadmap for reproducible releases.
